title: Dedicated: implement GPU-seconds meter v2 + schema + shadow-compare mode
author: Ethan Park
body: Context: We’ve had recurring Dedicated invoice questions where GPU usage appears overstated/under-explained when pools autoscale or when nodes sit idle between workloads (see SUP-28505). The existing meter (v1) is difficult to reconcile because it mixes control-plane state transitions with per-node sampling and doesn’t preserve enough attribution to explain “why did we bill X GPU-seconds?” This PR introduces GPU-seconds meter v2 with clearer, auditable rules, a new schema that preserves the underlying time slices, and a shadow-compare mode that computes v1 and v2 in parallel without impacting invoices. What changes: (1) Meter definition v2: GPU-seconds are computed as the integral of (allocated_gpus) over time for a Dedicated pool, segmented by allocation_state with explicit treatment for idle. “Allocated” is defined as GPUs bound to the customer’s pool by the autoscaler/control plane (not request-level utilization). v2 accounts for autoscaling transitions using bounded intervals derived from pool_allocation_events; sampling gaps are capped and flagged (see “gap handling” below). (2) Schema changes: adds a dedicated usage slice table and a daily rollup for Finance/RevRec reconciliation. New tables: billing.dedicated_gpu_seconds_slices_v2 (one row per {account_id,pool_id,node_id,interval_start,interval_end,state,gpu_count,gpu_type,region,cluster_id,meter_version}) and billing.dedicated_gpu_seconds_daily_v2 (daily aggregates by {account_id,pool_id,region,gpu_type}). The existing billing.dedicated_gpu_seconds_daily (v1) is unchanged. (3) Shadow compare mode: feature flag billing.dedicated_gpu_seconds.shadow_compare_enabled causes the pipeline to compute both v1 and v2 aggregates and emit a comparison record (billing.dedicated_gpu_seconds_shadow_diff) keyed by {account_id,pool_id,day}. The diff table stores v1_gpu_seconds, v2_gpu_seconds, pct_diff, top_diff_reason, and data_quality flags. This is intended for at least a 2-week bake before any invoicing switch. (4) Observability + data quality: emits counters for “allocation event gap capped”, “negative/overlapping interval fixed”, and “missing node GPU count fallback”. Adds Grafana-friendly metrics and structured logs with pool_id/account_id tags behind existing PII guards. Gap handling: v2 converts discrete allocation events into non-overlapping intervals. If we observe a gap between events > max_gap_seconds (default 120s), we cap billing at max_gap_seconds and mark the slice gap_capped=true; this prevents runaway overbilling on missing events and makes gaps obvious in recon. We also hard-fail (and page) if a pool has > N capped gaps per hour (configured in the job). Notes for Finance/RevRec: No invoice impact in this PR by default; v2 runs only when shadow_compare_enabled is true. We are explicitly not backfilling historical invoices here. Follow-up will be a Finance/Legal-approved change control to switch the billing source from v1 to v2 after shadow diffs are within thresholds. Test coverage: unit tests for intervalization (overlap, reorder, duplicate events), golden tests on known autoscale traces, and an end-to-end job test that materializes slices + daily rollup for a synthetic pool with scale up/down + idle + missing event gap. Rollout plan: deploy behind flag in staging for 48h, then enable in prod for 10% of pools (hash by pool_id) for 3 days, then 100% shadow compare. Any v2/v1 diff > 2% (daily, per pool) will generate a Slack alert to #finance and #eng-sre with a link to the diff row and the runbook. Checklist: [x] Schema migrations gated and reversible [x] Shadow diff table documented [x] Alerts added for data-quality flags [x] Finance review of definitions (Emily/Laura async) [x] SRE runbook link added to alert annotations.
commits: dedicated/billing: add v2 intervalization + slice model
billing/schema: add dedicated_gpu_seconds_slices_v2 + daily_v2 + shadow_diff tables
billing/job: compute v2 rollups + shadow compare output (flag gated)
tests: add golden traces for autoscaling transitions + gap handling
obs: add metrics/log fields for v2 data-quality signals
test_plan: Unit: dedicated_gpu_seconds_v2 intervalization tests (overlap/duplicate/out-of-order events, negative durations, long gaps). Golden: replay 6 captured autoscaler traces (scale up/down, node replacement, idle windows) and assert expected slices + totals. E2E: run metering job in CI with seeded events; validate v1 unchanged and v2 writes slices/daily/shadow diff when flag enabled. Manual: staging run against a real Dedicated pool for 2 hours; compare v1 vs v2 daily totals and spot-check slices around scale transitions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge + deploy to staging with shadow_compare_enabled=true; monitor capped-gap metrics and job latency. 2) Prod canary: enable shadow compare for 10% pools via config (hash pool_id) for 72 hours. 3) Expand to 100% shadow compare; keep invoicing on v1. 4) After Finance sign-off (separate change request): switch invoice source table to v2 daily rollup + retain v1 for audit for 90 days.
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): Intervalization logic looks good. Question: why cap gaps at 120s instead of treating as unknown and excluding entirely? We should be explicit about bias direction.

Ethan Park (author): Cap is intended as a safety valve against missing events causing runaway billing. Excluding entirely biases under-billing but hides data loss; with cap+flag we both bound impact and surface the issue. Added rationale to runbook + metric + alert on excessive capped gaps.
Nadia Rahman (review): Can we ensure slices are non-overlapping per {pool_id,node_id}? Also, please include meter_version in both slice and daily schemas so recon can join cleanly.

Ethan Park (author): Added a normalization step that sorts + merges contiguous intervals of same state and asserts no overlap; also added meter_version column + included in primary keys/indices where appropriate.
Emily Stone (Finance/RevRec): For shadow compare, can you include a single ‘top_diff_reason’ field we can use in triage (idle-accounting change vs gap-capped vs missing node metadata)?
Ethan Park (author): Added top_diff_reason enum derivation in the shadow diff writer, plus a data_quality_flags array in logs (table stores a comma-separated string to keep schema simple).

Mei Lin (review): Indexing: daily_v2 will be hit by Finance exports and drift checks. Please add composite index on (day, account_id) and (account_id, pool_id, day). Also, update schema docs with retention expectations.
Ethan Park (author): Added both indices and updated billing_tables.md with 400-day retention for slices (subject to policy) and 7-year for daily aggregates; slices remain restricted-access.

Aisha Bello (SRE): Alert tuning: paging on >2% diff seems noisy during initial rollout. Suggest warn-only for first week and page only if diff >5% OR absolute delta > 50k GPU-seconds for an account-day.
Ethan Park (author): Adjusted alert rule to warn at 2% and page at (pct_diff>5% AND abs_delta>50k) or capped_gap_rate above threshold. Added annotation linking to the new runbook.
Cole Summers (review): One concern: shadow compare job writes extra rows; ensure it doesn’t slow down month-end processing. Any perf numbers?
Ethan Park (author): Added simple perf benchmark in description: +6–9% runtime on a 24h backfill slice set in staging. Also ensured shadow diff writes are batched and can be disabled independently.
release_notes: Added Dedicated GPU-seconds metering v2 (shadow mode) with auditable time-slice schema
Introduced shadow diff outputs for Finance/Eng reconciliation without invoice impact
Added data-quality metrics/alerts for allocation event gaps and interval anomalies
